      "observations": [
        "All four owned files were read. The document adds the Fluent resource, the displayed/active count becomes m/n arguments, and the facet List all label gets the total ordered-group count. Other property-bundle strings remain. Original items-m-of-n repeats the m selector in all nested branches; accepted source instead uses item-count-m-of-n with direct m/n interpolation. No all-locale equivalent output is assumed.",
        "The original recipient rewrite reads identity.name, builds a sliced contactNames list of at most two entries, tests that length > 3, then ignores that list and formats a separately mapped full array. The capped-list branch is therefore unreachable as written. The original toggles separator classes by position instead of inspecting Intl part.type. It does not implement the intended old three-recipient-and-others contract.",
        "The inspected Gloda recipients registration is nonsingular and identity-valued. GlodaIdentity exposes contact and uses contact.name for its display; its complete identity implementation and the recipient attribute window are byte-identical at this original revision and the fixed comparison. Accepted rendering later uses recipient.contact?.name, filters nameless recipients, caps three names, computes omitted count from all recipients, formats that same list and classifies element versus literal parts.",
        "The original changes no tests or assertions. Later accepted tests use minimal gloda-like fixtures and directly assert capped names, singular/plural others, unnamed-recipient accounting, separator nodes and To text. Those later fixture assertions are separate from this original patch and were not executed. No actual indexed message, locale or accessibility run occurred.",
        "The original complete Bug 1935334 family context is reused. Own D280640 has no submitted inlines or summary edits. Initial approval precedes the apply-cleanly complaint, author rebase and landing with ongoing or failed builds. The vague no-recipe rationale is not an accepted general rule and does not resolve the original recipient-cap/data-field defects. Later accepted rendering and fixture assertions remain separate phases."
